verdict_reasoning: No surviving objection questions the goal, and reviewers in messages #2 and #14 accept the helper. Two fixable points remain. maintenance-fit-1: with even_if_detached false the helper returns InvalidOid, while get_partition_parent() raises an error. demand-1: the callers that would settle that contract are in the unmerged EXCEPT patches. A committer who knows the partition detach code needs to decide the contract.

brief.title: Add C function get_partition_root, equivalent of pg_partition_root
brief.problem: Backend code that needs only the root of a partition tree must fetch and free a full ancestors list and take llast_oid(ancestors). The author expects many more such call sites in the in-development FOR TABLES IN SCHEMA EXCEPT logical replication patches.
brief.proposed_design: The patch adds get_partition_root() in partition.c, used by pg_partition_root() and pg_depend.c. It takes an even_if_detached flag, like get_partition_parent(), and returns InvalidOid when a concurrent detach is pending. In v7, check_rel_can_be_partition() becomes shared code, and both get_partition_root() and get_partition_ancestors() check their input with Assert.
user_visible_surface: C API: new get_partition_root(relid, even_if_detached) in catalog/partition.h.
C API: check_rel_can_be_partition() moves from partitionfuncs.c to common code.
C API: get_partition_ancestors() gains Assert-based input checks in v7.
author_claims: Removes the need to build and free an ancestors list just to get the root.
Will simplify many call sites in the FOR TABLES IN SCHEMA EXCEPT patches.
The CommitFest entry tags it "Refactoring Only".
brief.thread_state: shveta malik, Chao Li and Álvaro Herrera reviewed it, and the v6 wrapper was dropped in v7 after Herrera's objection. Open: Assert versus if/elog validation, catalog lookups inside Assert, and whether a pending detach with even_if_detached false should raise an error or return InvalidOid.
unclear: Herrera asked whether validation should be if/elog, and the thread has no answer from him on v7.
The patch does not say how callers should tell a dropped relation from a non-partition.
Message #11 says existing get_partition_ancestors() callers may crash during a detach, and the thread does not say whether that is fixed or out of scope.
The thread does not show whether "Refactoring Only" still holds, since v7 changes get_partition_ancestors() checks.
The thread does not show whether other committers support adding this helper before the EXCEPT patches land.

objections.title: Main demand rests on unmerged EXCEPT patches; two callers today
objections.failure_scenario: A committer pushes get_partition_root() with its even_if_detached flag and InvalidOid-on-detach behaviour. The FOR TABLES IN SCHEMA EXCEPT patches then change shape or stall. Core is left with an exported helper whose detach semantics were never checked against the callers it was designed for.
objections.argument: In core, only pg_partition_root() and one site in pg_depend.c use the helper. Message #1 justifies it mainly by "many more code fragments" in the EXCEPT patches, which are "still in development". Message #2 also ties it to that patch. Messages #17 and #20 leave the detach behaviour open, and only real callers can settle whether an error or InvalidOid is the right answer.
objections.author_must_show: Which EXCEPT call sites would use get_partition_root(), and how does each one handle a pending detach, ideally shown as patch 0001 of that series?

critic.reasoning: Herrera's "looks okay" and shveta malik's support lower the doubt about desirability, but neither names the EXCEPT call sites. The detach contract is still open in message #20, and those callers are the evidence that would settle it.

objections.title: Detach-pending case returns InvalidOid, unlike get_partition_parent
objections.failure_scenario: An EXCEPT-patch caller writes relid = get_partition_root(relid, false) and passes the result to a syscache lookup or table_open. During an ALTER TABLE ... DETACH PARTITION CONCURRENTLY, it gets InvalidOid, and the failure shows up as an odd 'cache lookup failed for relation 0' or a silent mismatch. Nobody sees it until a user hits the race in production.
objections.argument: Chao Li approved even_if_detached because it matches get_partition_parent() (message #12). With false, get_partition_parent() raises an error, but the new helper returns InvalidOid. Message #4 shows a caller pattern, relid = get_partition_root(relid), that assigns the result without checking it. The thread lists this as open (message #20), and no committer has answered. A helper meant for many future callers should not need each caller to remember a sentinel check when its sibling function raises an error instead.
objections.author_must_show: Why should get_partition_root(relid, false) return InvalidOid instead of erroring like get_partition_parent(), and how will callers be kept from using the result unchecked?

critic.reasoning: Message #20 lists this as open, and no committer has answered. get_partition_parent() raises an error in the same case, so the departure needs a stated reason.

refuted.title: Helper and its contract are justified by callers that are not yet committed
refuted.failure_scenario: The helper is committed with two callers. The EXCEPT patches then change shape or stall. The tree is left with a new exported function, new Assert checks in get_partition_ancestors(), and detach semantics that no one has measured against the real callers.
refuted.argument: In tree, the helper replaces llast_oid(ancestors) at two sites, pg_partition_root() and pg_depend.c (message #1). The remaining benefit depends on patches 'still in development' (message #1), and shveta malik ties the timing to them (message #2). Since v7 the patch also changes get_partition_ancestors() checks, so the 'Refactoring Only' tag is less accurate. A committer would likely prefer to commit this as patch 0001 of the EXCEPT series, so its contract is decided against real callers.
refuted.author_must_show: Which call sites in the EXCEPT patches use get_partition_root(), and why commit it now and not as the first patch of that series?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of demand-1. Its one extra point, the "Refactoring Only" tag, concerns Assert-only checks that do nothing in production builds and has no failure scenario.

refuted.title: Helper duplicates the llast_oid idiom with only two callers today
refuted.failure_scenario: The helper lands now, but the FOR TABLES IN SCHEMA EXCEPT series changes or stalls. Core then has two ways to get the root, and they behave differently during a pending detach. Future callers pick one without guidance, so detach handling differs by call site.
refuted.argument: get_partition_ancestors() followed by llast_oid() already gives the root. The patch converts only pg_depend.c and pg_partition_root(), so the gain is one list allocation at two call sites. The main justification, per message #1 and message #2, is a patch series still in development. Message #11 notes the existing ancestors callers have their own detach hazard, which this helper leaves in place.
refuted.author_must_show: Could the helper be committed together with the EXCEPT patches that need it, or convert every existing llast_oid(get_partition_ancestors()) caller in core?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of demand-1: same stall scenario and same request to commit with the EXCEPT series. Its point about differing detach behaviour is covered by maintenance-fit-1.

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: The patch exports get_partition_root() in catalog/partition.h and moves check_rel_can_be_partition() to shared code.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: Core gets a second way to find the root, and its pending-detach behaviour differs from get_partition_parent().

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Why does get_partition_root(relid, false) return InvalidOid during a pending detach instead of raising an error like get_partition_parent()?
Which call sites in the FOR TABLES IN SCHEMA EXCEPT patches would use get_partition_root(), and what does each one do when a detach is pending?
Should input validation use if/elog instead of Assert, as Álvaro Herrera asked, given that the Assert checks do catalog lookups?
How does a caller tell a dropped relation from a relation that is not a partition?
Does the patch fix the crash risk that message #11 reports for existing get_partition_ancestors() callers during a detach, or is that out of scope?

committability.owner_note: Álvaro Herrera reviewed the patch and his objection led to v7, but the thread shows no reply from him on v7. The owner needs to know the DETACH PARTITION CONCURRENTLY code.
committability.liability: The owner signs for the pending-detach contract of an exported helper that the EXCEPT patches and extensions may call. Changing that contract later means auditing every caller.
committability.author_follow_up: The author posted seven versions in response to reviews and moved the entry to the next CommitFest.

priority.reason: The patch is about 9 KiB over four files and has two callers in core today. Its main users are the unmerged EXCEPT patches, so reviewing it as the first patch of that series would settle the detach contract against real callers.

provisional_note: The code was not read and only 3 of 20 messages were shown. Two points are unchecked: which even_if_detached value pg_partition_root() passes, and whether its result changes for a partition under a pending detach.

precedents_retrieved.title: Re: BUG #18741: Detaching a partition referencing a partitioned table fails with a trigger-related error
precedents_retrieved.summary: Alexander Lakhin reported that detaching a partition fails with an internal trigger error when the partition has a foreign key to a partitioned table and its new parent has no matching foreign key. Tender Wang and jian he discussed fixing this, mainly by rejecting such ATTACH PARTITION commands except where the partition references a non-partitioned table or its own parent's hierarchy.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. They contain the bug report and two design suggestions with no patch, review or decision, and they do not say why the entry was withdrawn.

precedents_retrieved.title: Prevent pg_basebackup running as root
precedents_retrieved.summary: Make pg_basebackup refuse to run as root (except for --help/--version), matching the existing checks in initdb, pg_ctl and pg_upgrade, so it cannot create root-owned files in a data directory that the postmaster could not use. The change was not to be backpatched, as it alters behavior.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The patch was committed by Michael Paquier and then reverted after a separate discussion that is linked but not included in the visible messages. The visible messages do not show why.

precedents_retrieved.title: Verify true root on replicas with amcheck
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets the regular bt_check_index() function in amcheck verify the true root of a B-Tree index, so the check also works on replicas. It does this by locking the metapage and the potential root page at the same time.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author stopped responding. Peter Geoghegan asked what true root corruption meant and what symptom it caused, and he did not want to commit a patch that holds multiple buffer locks without a strong justification. The patch also stopped applying, and David Steele returned it after no reply from the author.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Your patch looks like it gets it right (it won't deadlock with other
sessions that access the metapage), but I hesitate to commit it
without a strong justification.

precedents_retrieved.title: Allow logical replication via inheritance root table
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets an extension or user mark an existing inheritance child so that logical replication publishes its changes through a chosen parent, reusing the publish_via_partition_root machinery. It adds a publisher-side function that tells the subscriber which tables to COPY during initial sync, and later a publish_via_parent reloption set with ALTER TABLE.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author paused the entry after finding that the subscriber side could not handle the routed data: when incoming tuples are moved to other tables, a later UPDATE or DELETE checks the root table and does not find the rows. He decided to work on subscriber-side support first. Amit Kapila also said that one extension's needs are not a reason to accept the feature in core.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Given that, I think I need to pivot and focus on the subscriber side first. That might(?) be a smaller effort anyway, and if we can't make headway there then publisher-side support probably doesn't make sense at all.

precedents_retrieved.title: Use ReadRecentBuffer() for btree root page
precedents_retrieved.summary: Cache the btree root page's buffer ID per relation and use ReadRecentBuffer() in _bt_getroot() to skip the buffer mapping lookup. To make that scale, ReadRecentBuffer() would pin with PinBuffer() instead of taking the buffer header spinlock, which also bumps the usage count.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andres Freund objected to keeping the cached root buffer in rd_amcache, because each access method would then duplicate the same code. He suggested putting the fields in RelationData instead. Thomas Munro answered with an experimental LRU of recent lookups, and Andres said that should be a separate facility. No revised patch followed, so in January 2024 the entry was set to Waiting on Author, and the visible messages show no reply after that.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I am wondering if we don't want something more generic than stashing this in rd_amcache.

precedents_retrieved.title: refactor ExecInitPartitionInfo
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch replaces the repeated lazy `if (part_attmap == NULL) build_attrmap_by_name(...)` calls in ExecInitPartitionInfo with a single up-front build. The build runs under one combined condition on the ModifyTable node, to reduce duplication before ON CONFLICT DO SELECT adds another use.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers found no real gain in performance or readability. The original code builds the attribute map lazily and keeps each build next to the remapping that needs it, while the central condition separates that knowledge and is easy to miss when a new path needs the map. Heikki Linnakangas agreed with this review and marked the entry rejected.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: With the consolidated version, we reduce a few repeated if (part_attmap == NULL) checks, but I do not think that gives us a meaningful improvement in either performance or readability.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add OID descriptions to dumped parse/query/plan trees
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds comments to the text dumps of parse, query and plan trees that name the object behind each OID, such as the index, operator, function or type. It does this by catalog lookups inside the node output code.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected that the lookups would make the dump code need a live, non-aborted transaction and could add catalog accesses that cause problems or deadlocks, so pprint could no longer be called from almost anywhere. He also said the change breaks re-reading of dumped trees, which rules, views and parallel query depend on. The author withdrew the patch after this reply.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
It means that the dump code has to
execute in a live (not-aborted) transaction, which is not a
requirement it had before, and will complicate some debugging
scenarios.

precedents_retrieved.title: [PATCH] Equivalence Class Filters
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds equivalence filters to equivalence classes, so a btree-operator clause of the form "Expr op Const", such as t1.id <= 10, is also applied to the other members of the class, such as t2.id. The planner collects these clauses while it builds the equivalence classes, then attaches each one to the class that contains its expression.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane said the matching search would cost planner cycles on every query, often for no gain, and that redundant derived clauses could skew selectivity estimates. Robert Haas showed that pushing the inequality to every relation can make execution slower, for example a retest on the inner side of a parameterized nested loop, and that choosing where to apply it is hard. David Rowley then said the patch was not wanted in its current form and that he would not work on it further.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I'm not necessarily opposed to doing anything in this area, but so far
I've not seen how to do it in a way that is attractive when planner
complexity, performance, and end results are all considered.

This reverts commit b0a55f4, to remove for now the TAP test that did the
equivalent of check_guc.  The test has been using pg_config --sharedir
to find the location of postgresql.conf.sample.  While the buildfarm and

for Debian where pg_config is patched to not be relocatable, causing the

issue as a TAP test only offers the build directory as of TESTDIR in the
environment context, so this would fail with VPATH builds.  Perhaps the
source path could be provided additionally when running the TAP tests.

approach, by using PG_ABS_SRCDIR but this is going to require some extra
loops to get the sample file from the correct path in src/backend/.  In
any case, this needs more thoughts, so just revert the test case until
something better is done about this relocation problem.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found for a C helper that returns a partition root. [P9] was a refactoring rejected for giving no readability gain, but this helper adds handling for a pending detach, and reviewers in messages #2 and #14 accept the idea. The open points in message #20 are design details, not a reason this idea died before.

The patch adds an internal C helper and changes no SQL syntax, GUC, catalog, pg_dump output or psql behaviour. The diff is not shown, so one point stays unchecked: which even_if_detached value pg_partition_root() passes, and whether its result for a partition under a pending DETACH CONCURRENTLY changes.

The patch adds a backend C helper and moves check_rel_can_be_partition() into shared code. Nothing changes on-disk format, WAL, catalogs, replication, the wire protocol or existing structs. The extension API change only adds functions, and detach-pending state is read, never written.

The proposal adds an internal C helper and moves validation code. pg_partition_root() keeps its SQL surface and privileges, so nothing changes in who can call what or what they can see. The Assert reachable from pg_partition_root() during a concurrent detach (message #10) affects only assert-enabled builds and was addressed in v5, so I see no privilege, exposure or denial-of-service aspect.
The helper adds no hot-path cost, because its checks are Assert-only, and it adds no external dependency. Álvaro Herrera has engaged, so the remaining concerns are API-level and fixable.
The objection is weak. Herrera called the approach okay in message #14, and the helper follows the even_if_detached convention of get_partition_parent().
Several reviewers support a root lookup helper, and Herrera called it okay in message #14. The only demand gap is that most of the expected callers are not yet in core.
